stimulus_db: Early urban societies could not have been maintained without large-scale farming nearby. This is because other methods of food acquisition, such as foraging, cannot support populations as dense as urban ones. Large-scale farming requires irrigation, which remained unfeasible in areas far from rivers or lakes until more recent times.
stem_db: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices_db.A: Most peoples who lived in early times lived in areas near rivers or lakes.
choices_db.B: Only if farming is possible in the absence of irrigation can societies be maintained in areas far from rivers or lakes.
choices_db.C: In early times it was not possible to maintain urban societies in areas far from rivers or lakes.
choices_db.D: Urban societies with farms near rivers or lakes do not have to rely upon irrigation to meet their farming needs.
choices_db.E: Early rural societies relied more on foraging than on agriculture for food.

steps.label: Given
steps.body:
Early urban societies could not have been maintained without large-scale farming nearby.
US → LSF

This is because other methods of food acquisition, such as foraging, cannot support populations as dense as urban ones.

Large-scale farming requires irrigation, which remained unfeasible in areas far from rivers or lakes until more recent times.
LSF → IR
~RL → ~IR

notes.body: Where people actually lived in early times is not discussed in the statements.
This goes too far by changing the subject from urban societies to societies more generally.

This follows from combining the three conditional statements.

~RL → ~IR
~IR → ~LSF
~LSF → ~US
∴ ~RL → ~US

Urban societies require large-scale farming, and large-scale farming requires irrigation.

US → LSF → IR

So urban societies with farms near rivers or lakes still rely on irrigation, which contradicts D.
Early rural societies are not discussed in the statements.
